summary: DEADLINE: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships & Leadership Programme (Oxford master's, 2027-28)
description:
Eligibility: Graduates and early-career professionals from mainly low- and middle-income countries; must be admitted to an eligible 1-year Oxford master's course (no DPhil) and intend to return to their home country or region. Most scholars have 5+ years of work experience, but it is not required. Check Oxford's lists of eligible countries and courses.
Benefits: 100% of course fees, a living stipend (£21,805 in 2026-27) and a place on the Leadership Programme (about 200 hours, mid-September to early July).
Deadline: Set by the Oxford course: the January deadline or earlier (some courses close in December). The date shown is a typical January date, so check your course page.
Requirements: Select the scholarship on the Oxford graduate application form and submit the WHT application at the same time; English language test required.
Portal: https://whtrust.org/scholarship-application/

summary: DEADLINE: OIST Research Internship Program (Japan) - Fall round
description:
Focus: Research internships hosted by OIST faculty units across science and technology. OIST lists current openings on its Faculty & Project Availability page.
Eligibility: Students in the last two years of a bachelor's degree (or who will be by the internship start), any year of a master's degree, or graduates with a bachelor's or master's. Enrolled students need approval from their home institution. Current or graduated PhD students are not eligible. It is meant for people who need more research experience and may want to join OIST's PhD Program later.
Requirements: Transcript and diploma (or an enrollment certificate), a statement of purpose (250 words max), CV, 1-3 recommendation letters from professorial-level faculty (lab members and postdocs do not count), passport and ID photo. An English test is optional.
Fee: 5,000 JPY, non-refundable, and OIST offers no waivers for personal financial situations.
Deadline: Apr 15, 23:59 JST for the Fall round (Apr 15, 2027 for the Oct 1, 2027 to Mar 31, 2028 period; results in mid-June). Internships last 4-6 months. OIST says the schedule is tentative.
Benefits: Not listed on the application page. An earlier version of this entry mentioned a daily allowance of about 2,400 JPY, so check the Program Description page for what is covered.
Portal: https://www.oist.jp/admissions/research-internship/apply-research-internship

summary: DEADLINE: Max Planck Institutes (CIS) Research Internship - Summer Start
description:

Eligibility: Bachelors, Masters and PhD students worldwide with roughly the first three years of a CS bachelors completed by the start, and an excellent academic record. Prior research experience is not required.

summary: DEADLINE: Gates Foundation AI Fellow - Africa Regional Offices (12-month fellowship)
description:
Eligibility: Early-to-mid-career professionals, per the program's 2026 page. This is a 12-month limited-term employment position, not a student program. Check the posting for the minimum degree and years of experience.
Location: Abuja (Nigeria), Addis Ababa (Ethiopia), Johannesburg (South Africa) or Nairobi (Kenya).
Focus: Apply AI to the Foundation's health, development and education priorities in low- and middle-income countries; each fellow is assigned 1-2 high-priority projects with the Africa team and partners.
Deadline: Apply by Nov 11, 2026 (the Workday listing closes Nov 12 EST).
Note: One-off call for the first Africa-based cohort. Pay for this cohort is not confirmed; the earlier global program listed about $148,920-$162,350 depending on location.
Portal: https://gatesfoundation.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/Gates/job/AI-Fellow---Africa-Regional-Offices_B021830-1

summary: DEADLINE: Max Planck CaCTüS Internship (Tübingen & Stuttgart)
description:
Focus: Computation and cognition (AI, machine learning and brain research) at the Max Planck Institutes for Biological Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems and the Tübingen AI Center.
Eligibility: Bachelor's and Master's students worldwide. The programme specifically targets motivated students constrained by personal, financial, regional or societal issues that affect their future education, and applicants are expected to explain how access to first-class education is constrained for them. Students from low- and middle-income countries are explicitly encouraged to apply. Students without a finished Bachelor's need at least 4 completed semesters (earlier years counted them at application, the 2026 page before the internship starts, so check the 2027 call).
Program: Paid 3-month research internship, Jul 1 to Sep 30, 2027. You must be available for the full period, and it must be voluntary rather than for course credit. The coordination office arranges affordable accommodation. The exact stipend and travel support are not confirmed here.
Deadline: Nov 16, 2026 (portal opened Oct 21; interviews in January, notifications in February). No application fee.
Portal: https://www.projects.tuebingen.mpg.de/

summary: DEADLINE: Summer @ EPFL Research Fellowship (Switzerland)
description:
Focus: Summer research projects in EPFL's School of Computer and Communication Sciences. You choose up to 3 domains, and no project list is published in advance.
Eligibility: Students enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme at another institution at the time of the fellowship. EPFL's own students are not eligible.
Requirements: CV, all university transcripts, and a 1-2 page motivation letter (PDF). Do not upload recommendation letters; the official page says they may jeopardize your application.
Deadline: Sunday Nov 29, 2026, 23:39 AoE. Offers come about 4-6 weeks after the deadline.
Note: You arrange your own accommodation (EPFL staff can suggest places). Stipend details are not confirmed here, so check the official page.
Portal: https://summer.epfl.ch/apply.html

summary: DEADLINE: EDSAFE AI Alliance Women in AI Fellowship (women only, part-time)
description:
Eligibility: Women technologists (AI, data science or related fields) and women educational leaders (administrators, teachers, researchers, policymakers) interested in the safe, ethical use of AI in education. Open worldwide, and self-nominations are welcome. The form asks for your organization and examples of your work, so it looks aimed at working professionals more than students.
Program: 12-month fellowship starting in January 2027, with virtual workshops, mentorship from past fellows, a cohort of 30+ people and a micro-capstone project. Expect about 2-4 hours a month.
Benefits: No participation cost. There is no honorarium or compensation.
Deadline: Nov 30, 2026, 10 p.m. EST (about 4 a.m. on Dec 1 in Nigeria). Fellows are announced in January 2027.
Portal: https://www.edsafeai.org/fellowship

summary: DEADLINE: ETH Zurich Student Summer Research Fellowship (SSRF)
description:
Focus: Research areas listed by ETH: Machine Learning, Information Security, Computer Systems, Robotics, Programming Languages and Software Engineering, Bio/Medical informatics, Human-computer interaction, Theory and Visual Computing.
Eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students worldwide, except students enrolled at ETH Zurich. The programme is aimed at students gaining their first research experience. Earlier calls also asked for an expected graduation date in the year after the fellowship or later, and availability for both summer months.
Benefits: Two summer months at ETH. The stipend is reported to cover travel, accommodation and living costs, so confirm on the call page.
Requirements: Academic transcript, CV and motivation letter, as listed in earlier calls.
Deadline: Applications reportedly run Nov 1 to Dec 16, 2026 (the 2024 cutoff was 13:00 CET). ETH's page had not been updated for the 2027 call when I checked, so confirm the date and time.
Portal: https://inf.ethz.ch/studies/summer-research-fellowship.html
